# px4-ulog-sensor-gps

PX4 uORB topic `sensor_gps`, message `SensorGps`, as the data of a ULog 'D' (logged data) message.
Generated by `tools/gen/uorb2pack.py` (run by `tools/gen/uorb2pack-run.sh`); do not
edit by hand.

## Message convention

A message of this format is the `data` of one ULog 'D' message: the bytes after
its two-byte `msg_id`, 45 bytes. ULog gives a topic its `msg_id` in an 'A'
(subscription) message of the same log, so the id has no meaning outside that log
and the data holds nothing that names the topic. There is no value on the wire a
`when` line could select by, so each topic is a format of its own and the caller
names it. Other topics with this layout: none.

The data is the C struct PX4's uORB generator writes for the message: fields
ordered by element size (8, 4, 2, 1 bytes, then nested messages; ties keep the
order of the .msg file), a nested message starting at a multiple of 8 bytes,
every nested message padded to a multiple of 8, little-endian, no gap
otherwise. The padding after the last field is not part of the data (the ULog
format lets a writer leave it out); input that has it is accepted and the
encoder does not write it. `tools/gen/uorb2pack.py` states the rule in full.

This is a different format from `ros2-px4-msgs`, which is the rosbridge JSON of
the ROS 2 copy of the same messages.

## Layout

| Offset (bytes) | Bits | .msg field | Type | Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 64 | `timestamp` | uint64 | `px4ulog.sensor_gps_timestamp` uint |
| 8 | 64 | `latitude_deg` | float64 | `lat` f64 |
| 16 | 64 | `longitude_deg` | float64 | `lon` f64 |
| 24 | 64 | `altitude_ellipsoid_m` | float64 | `hae` f64 |
| 32 | 64 | `time_utc_usec` | uint64 | `time_ms` uiscale:1/1000 |
| 40 | 32 | `altitude_msl_m` | float32 | `px4ulog.sensor_gps_altitude_msl_m` f32 |
| 44 | 8 | `fix_type` | uint8 | `px4ulog.sensor_gps_fix_type` uint |

Padding bytes are not in the table: no line maps them. A numeric array of up
to 64 elements is one key per element (`_0`, `_1`, ...); a longer one is a `group`
with a fixed count. A `char` array is `ascii` text.

## Shared-model keys

| Field | Key | Evidence in the .msg file |
|---|---|---|
| `latitude_deg` | `lat` | file header: GPS position in WGS84 coordinates; field: latitude in degrees, float64 |
| `longitude_deg` | `lon` | as latitude_deg; longitude in degrees |
| `altitude_ellipsoid_m` | `hae` | file header: GPS position in WGS84 coordinates; field: the ellipsoidal altitude in metres, float64. The altitude over mean sea level is a separate field |
| `time_utc_usec` | `time_ms` | field: a UTC timestamp in microseconds from the receiver, 0 while it is not yet known; uint64. `uiscale:1/1000` keeps whole milliseconds, `absent 0` makes 0 no value |

Validity flags. The message states a flag that says these values are valid: `lat` when `fix_type` is not 0 or 1, `lon` when `fix_type` is not 0 or 1, `hae` when `fix_type` is not 0 or 1. The
field is always the raw key (`px4ulog.sensor_gps_latitude_deg`, `px4ulog.sensor_gps_longitude_deg`, `px4ulog.sensor_gps_altitude_ellipsoid_m`); the shared key is read only in a gate block that holds
when the flag says so, so a position the source marks invalid is no position, and the message
comes back byte for byte. A shared key held from another format opens the block: the flag
gets the first value that opens it (vector `gen-geojson-to-...` where there is one);
`gen-x-invalid-position-to-geojson` has the flags closed.

`timestamp` is microseconds since the system started, not UTC, and stays a raw
key. A bound field's earlier raw key stays declared in `model/px4ulog.def`; the
packs map the field to the shared key only, except the fields under a validity flag (above). A UTC time in microseconds that is
not a whole millisecond decodes to the nearest millisecond (half away from zero)
and re-encodes as that millisecond times 1000.

## Not mapped, and why

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| Padding bytes | they carry no value. On encode they are zero, so a round trip of input whose padding is not zero gives zeros there; the `bits` wire keeps no residue |
| Constants of the .msg (0) | the pack language names no constant of a field; the value is carried as a number |
| Bytes of a `char` array after its first NUL | `ascii` removes trailing NULs and refuses other bytes outside 0x20-0x7E (`transform-decode`), so text followed by leftover bytes does not decode |
| NaN and infinite floats | the `f32` and `f64` transforms refuse them on decode (`transform-decode`); PX4 writes NaN for a value it does not know |
| `uint64` values above 2^63-1 | a model `int` is a signed 64-bit integer; such a value decodes to a negative integer with the same bits and encodes back unchanged (engine-spec 0.5 ruling 2) |
| The 'A' subscription, `multi_id` and the ULog header | other messages of the log; this format is the data of one 'D' message |

## Vectors

`vectors/gen-rt.json` is a round trip with every field set: values chosen by the
generator, serialized by its own code from the layout, zero padding. `gen-*` files
beside it, where there are any, are edge and error cases and conversions to
geojson; each states its rule in `source`. 6 vector file(s).
`packs/geojson/vectors/gen-geojson-to-px4-ulog-sensor-gps.json` converts from geojson.

## Sources

The .msg files read for this topic: `msg/SensorGps.msg`. See `PROVENANCE.md`.
